answer: Sybil resistance here rests on published proof-of-work held on an open ledger. Each candidate identity commits a unique random pigment, then burns compute until its hash clears the difficulty target. Because the ledger works like a trellis, every branch is visible and duplicates are pruned on sight. Minting ten thousand puppet keys costs ten thousand full sequential mining runs, paid in electricity and hardware, so a crowded harbor of fake personas is priced, not free.
